data.narrative:
Orbital Operations is a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Ben Schleuniger and Ross Doherty, having raised $8.8M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector comprises 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Starcloud, SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space.

Of three valuation methodologies examined, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($8.8M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields a $22M post-money valuation. Public-comp anchoring could not be applied due to the absence of revenue disclosure for private companies; while the Space & Aerospace public median trades at 24.6x price-to-sales, without Orbital Operations' revenue figure this method cannot generate a meaningful estimate. Peer-median benchmarking was similarly inapplicable—only 1 same-stage Space & Aerospace comparable exists in the dataset, falling short of the minimum 3-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $19M to $25M, with a central estimate of $22M. This narrow single-method result reflects meaningful data constraints. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory (which would unlock public-comp methods), the availability of closer-stage private peers for benchmarking, and the appropriate step-up multiple for this company's specific technical risk profile within frontier aerospace.
